draft.title: Properties of hydrocarbons
card: Hydrocarbons are non-polar molecules. The only forces between their molecules are weak dispersion forces.
A longer chain has more electrons and more surface contact between molecules. So dispersion forces are stronger and the boiling point is higher.
Small hydrocarbons such as methane are gases at room temperature. Longer chains are liquids, and very long chains are waxy solids.
Water molecules are polar and hold each other with strong hydrogen bonds. Hydrocarbons cannot form these bonds with water, so they do not dissolve in it.
draft.remember: Longer chain, stronger dispersion forces, higher boiling point. Non-polar hydrocarbons do not mix with polar water.

a.q: Why does pentane have a higher boiling point than propane?
opts: Its stronger dispersion forces need more energy to overcome
Its covalent bonds between carbons are stronger
It forms hydrogen bonds between its molecules
It has polar bonds that attract other molecules
a.why: Pentane has a longer chain, so its dispersion forces between molecules are stronger and more energy is needed to separate them. Boiling does not break the covalent bonds inside the molecules, so stronger bonds are not the reason.
a.clue: Think about the forces between molecules, not inside them.

b.q: Hexane is added to water in a test tube and shaken. What is seen after it settles, and why?
opts: Two layers, because hexane is non-polar and water is polar
Two layers, because hexane forms hydrogen bonds with itself
One layer, because hexane has dispersion forces like water
One layer, because hexane is a small molecule
b.why: Hexane is non-polar and cannot form hydrogen bonds with water, so the two do not mix and form layers. Dispersion forces exist in water too, but they are not enough to replace the strong hydrogen bonds between water molecules.
b.clue: Compare the polarity of hexane with the polarity of water.

a.best: Its stronger dispersion forces need more energy to overcome

b.best: Two layers, because hexane is non-polar and water is polar
